findings.reason: The protected implementation is concise, conventional, and expert-interview ready. The equality fast path makes the zero-operation exception explicit; mapping, source, and target communicate the functional-mapping invariant directly; conflict rejection is local and easy to explain; and the final 26-letter condition states the spare-label theorem without graph simulation or unnecessary helpers. No material clarity, correctness, or complexity improvement warrants a candidate.

A global conversion cannot separate occurrences that currently share a character, so each original source character must align with one target character; the scan rejects exactly a conflicting destination while correctly allowing several sources to merge. Equal strings require no operation. Otherwise, an absent target letter provides temporary storage for cycles, while a target containing all 26 letters leaves no spare and a consistent nonidentity mapping becomes a permutation containing an unbreakable cycle. Therefore the implementation's equality, mapping-consistency, and target-cardinality checks are jointly necessary and sufficient.

A breadth-first oracle explicitly enumerated global replacement states over a four-letter operation alphabet for every source/target pair of lengths 1 through 5 drawn from three target letters: 66,429 pairs in total. Protected and native results matched every reachable-state verdict. A separately structured pairwise-consistency oracle also matched six full-alphabet edge cases and 10,000 deterministic random lowercase pairs generated with seed 1153.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1153, Python, and native entrypoint Solution.canConvert. Authenticated source evidence confirms equal-length lowercase strings, zero or more conversions, replacement of all current occurrences by any other lowercase character, and a boolean feasibility result. It contains exactly two explained examples, two constraints, and six hints. solve(str1, str2) preserves that contract.

The immutable native source remains byte-for-byte bound to verified submission 2067858542. Apart from the required class/method wrapper and app-local mapping annotation, native and protected sources share the same equality return, aligned zipped scan, conflict condition, mapping assignment, and distinct-target test. Neither source nor submission.json changed during review.

The equality comparison, aligned mapping scan, and target-character set construction each inspect at most n positions, establishing O(n) time. The mapping and set each contain at most the fixed 26-letter alphabet, establishing O(1) auxiliary space with respect to n. Both manifest bounds are met.

The unchanged hidden tiers scale consistent cyclic mappings from 24 through 96 to 384 positions, a 16x span that avoids early rejection and exercises the complete linear scan. The exact protected source passed all 10 ordinary cases, all three benchmark outputs, and scaling at a 0.99x largest runtime ratio and +0.02 extra growth exponent. The independently correct pairwise-control source passed every output but failed only scaling at 110.90x and +1.41. benchmark.json required no edit.

The Approach exactly matches the protected equality fast path, source-to-target mapping construction, conflict rejection, target-letter cardinality test, and return value. It derives why merges are allowed, why a spare label opens conversion cycles, why all 26 target letters block a nonidentity permutation, and why the bounded alphabet gives O(1) auxiliary space. Its alternatives and edge cases cover every material branch.

The modular Reference preserves the equal-length input model, global all-occurrences replacement, other-character requirement, zero-or-more operations, order-sensitive intermediate strings, exact two examples and both explanations, both constraints, and all six hints in source order. It introduces no source-absent example, note, follow-up, table, image, or diagram.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed exactly two explained examples, two constraints, six hints, no tables, no images, and no diagrams. source_fidelity.json binds every modular section to live statement hash 40a0bd66e51ac1cc5982037a45d5c2f27d579ca4f0b3211424ac36fe7566857e and validates without errors.

coverage: sample-1 and sample-2 are the only authenticated source examples and preserve both exact input/output pairs. Their explanations retain the c-to-e, b-to-d, a-to-c sequence and its order dependence, and the impossibility statement for leetcode versus codeleet. The former invented sample-3 is correctly labelled as a trial.

All 10 ordinary fixtures are visible samples or trials. They cover n = 1 and n = 10000, zero-operation equality with the full alphabet, a one-character conversion, one source mapping to two targets, legal many-to-one merging, an ordered chain, a cycle with a spare letter, a full 26-letter cycle without a spare, and the 25-distinct-target boundary that restores a spare.

An independent pairwise oracle tests every pair of aligned positions rather than building a mapping. It agreed with all 10 expected results, exact protected bytes, exact immutable native bytes, and the slower benchmark control. The maximum-length fixture exposes its contradiction immediately so the intentionally quadratic control remains a correctness witness rather than timing out on an ordinary case.

A BFS conversion oracle exhaustively explored 66,429 source/target pairs over lengths 1 through 5 with an explicit spare operation character. Another 10,000 deterministic schema-valid lowercase pairs generated with seed 1153 covered varied lengths, repeated characters, merges, conflicts, equal strings, chains, and cycles. Protected and native sources matched every verdict.

The hidden performance-only tiers use common string length consistently as size, span 16x from 24 through 384, and retain one spare target letter while forcing a complete scan. Protected passed scaling at +0.02 and 0.99x; the correct O(n^2) pairwise control passed every output and failed only scaling at +1.41 and 110.90x. benchmark.json remained unchanged.
